Immunization & EPI.question: 1) Expanded Programme on Immunization was launched globally by WHO in:
Immunization & EPI.exp: EPI was launched globally by WHO in May 1974. It was introduced to expand routine vaccination services. Bangladesh started EPI later in 1979.

Immunization & EPI.question: 2) EPI started in Bangladesh on:
Immunization & EPI.exp: Bangladesh started EPI on 7th April 1979. This is a direct recall point from the file. WHO launched global EPI in May 1974.

Immunization & EPI.question: ৩) The EPI summary is:
Immunization & EPI.exp:
The EPI summary is 6 vaccines, 6 visits and 10 diseases.
This is a compact recall formula. It helps remember the routine EPI framework.

Immunization & EPI.question: 4) Vaccine given at birth in the EPI schedule is:
Immunization & EPI.exp: BCG is given at birth in the EPI schedule. It is a live attenuated vaccine. Other vaccines start from 6 weeks.

Immunization & EPI.question: 5) At 6 weeks, the EPI schedule includes Penta-1, OPV-1, PCV-1 and:
Immunization & EPI.exp: At 6 weeks, vaccines are Penta-1, OPV-1, PCV-1 and IPV-1. This is the first major infant EPI visit after birth. The same visit starts multiple primary series.

Immunization & EPI.question: 6) At 10 weeks, the EPI schedule includes:
Immunization & EPI.exp: At 10 weeks, Penta-2, OPV-2 and PCV-2 are given. IPV is not listed at the 10-week visit in the file. The next IPV dose appears at 14 weeks.

Immunization & EPI.question: 7) At 14 weeks, the EPI schedule includes Penta-3, OPV-3, PCV-3 and:
Immunization & EPI.exp: At 14 weeks, vaccines include Penta-3, OPV-3, PCV-3 and IPV-2. This completes the primary series listed in the file. IPV-1 is given earlier at 6 weeks.

Immunization & EPI.question: 8) MR-1 is given at:
Immunization & EPI.exp: MR-1 is given at 9 months. It is the first measles-rubella vaccine dose in the file schedule. MR-2 is given later at 15 months.

Immunization & EPI.question: 9) MR-2 is given at:
Immunization & EPI.exp: MR-2 is given at 15 months. MR-1 is given at 9 months. Both are combined vaccines in the file.

Immunization & EPI.question: 10) BCG and OPV are examples of:
Immunization & EPI.exp: The file lists BCG and OPV as live attenuated vaccines. Live vaccines contain weakened organisms. They generally produce strong immune response.

Immunization & EPI.question: 11) IPV is classified as:
Immunization & EPI.exp: IPV is listed as a killed vaccine. It is different from OPV, which is live attenuated. Both are used against poliomyelitis.

Immunization & EPI.question: 12) PCV is classified as:
Immunization & EPI.exp: PCV is listed under extracted cellular fraction vaccines. It is not live like BCG or OPV. It is included in the infant EPI schedule.

Immunization & EPI.question: 13) Penta and MR are classified as:
Immunization & EPI.exp: The file lists Penta and MR as combined vaccines. Combined vaccines contain more than one antigen. They reduce number of injections/visits.

Immunization & EPI.question: 14) Which pair is correctly matched?
Immunization & EPI.exp: PCV is listed as an extracted cellular fraction vaccine. BCG and OPV are live attenuated. IPV is killed, while Penta and MR are combined.

Immunization & EPI.question: 15) EPI Plus means:
Immunization & EPI.option1: Special services added to routine EPI platform
Immunization & EPI.exp: EPI Plus means extra services through the EPI platform. It does not replace routine vaccination. It adds child, couple and maternal services.

Immunization & EPI.question: 16) Vitamin A capsule for under-5 children is included under:
Immunization & EPI.exp: Vitamin A capsule for under-5 children is listed under EPI Plus. It is delivered through the EPI platform. It is not itself a routine vaccine.

Immunization & EPI.question: 17) Deworming programme under EPI Plus is directed mainly to:
Immunization & EPI.exp: Deworming programme is listed under child services in EPI Plus. Vitamin A is also included for children. EPI Plus expands child health services beyond vaccination.

Immunization & EPI.question: 18) Advice on breastfeeding under EPI Plus is listed for:
Immunization & EPI.exp: EPI Plus includes advice on breastfeeding for couple/mother. It also includes sex education and family planning advice. These are added services through routine EPI contact.

Immunization & EPI.question: 19) Family planning advice under EPI Plus is listed for:
Immunization & EPI.exp: Family planning advice is included under couple/mother services. EPI contact can be used for counseling. This increases integration of preventive services.

Immunization & EPI.question: 20) TT-1 gives protection for:
Immunization & EPI.exp: TT-1 has no protection duration in the file schedule. It starts the series. Protection begins properly after subsequent doses.

Immunization & EPI.question: 21) Minimum interval between TT-1 and TT-2 is:
Immunization & EPI.exp: TT-2 is given 4 weeks after TT-1. TT-2 provides protection for 3 years. This is the first protective dose in the schedule.

Immunization & EPI.question: 22) TT-2 gives protection for:
Immunization & EPI.exp: TT-2 protects for 3 years. Minimum interval from TT-1 is 4 weeks. Protection increases with later doses.

Immunization & EPI.question: 23) Minimum interval between TT-2 and TT-3 is:
Immunization & EPI.exp: TT-3 is given 6 months after TT-2. TT-3 gives 5 years protection. This is longer protection than TT-2.

Immunization & EPI.question: 24) TT-3 gives protection for:
Immunization & EPI.exp: TT-3 gives 5 years protection. Its minimum interval is 6 months after TT-2. TT-4 and TT-5 provide longer protection.

Immunization & EPI.question: 25) TT-4 is given after TT-3 at minimum interval of:
Immunization & EPI.exp: TT-4 is given 1 year after TT-3. It gives 10 years protection. The schedule then continues to TT-5.

Immunization & EPI.question: 26) TT-4 gives protection for:
Immunization & EPI.exp: TT-4 provides 10 years protection. The minimum interval from TT-3 is 1 year. TT-5 provides lifelong protection.

Immunization & EPI.question: 27) TT-5 gives protection for:
Immunization & EPI.exp: TT-5 provides lifelong protection. It is given 1 year after TT-4. This completes the TT schedule for women of reproductive age.

Immunization & EPI.question: 28) Minimum interval between TT-4 and TT-5 is:
Immunization & EPI.exp: TT-5 is given 1 year after TT-4. This dose gives lifelong protection. The interval is same as TT-4 after TT-3.

Immunization & EPI.question: 29) Polio and measles vaccines must be stored in:
Immunization & EPI.exp: The file states polio and measles vaccines must be stored in the freezer compartment. Other vaccines should be kept in cold part. They should not be allowed to freeze.

Immunization & EPI.question: 30) The rest of the vaccines except polio and measles should be stored in:
Immunization & EPI.option2: Cold part but never allowed to freeze
Immunization & EPI.exp: Most vaccines should be kept in the cold part. They must not be frozen. Freezing can damage freeze-sensitive vaccines.

Immunization & EPI.question: 31) Maximum storage temperature for any vaccine mentioned in the file is:
Immunization & EPI.exp: The maximum storage temperature for any vaccine is 8°C. This is part of cold chain maintenance. Vaccines should be protected from heat damage.

Immunization & EPI.question: 32) The usual cold chain temperature range for vaccines is:
Immunization & EPI.exp: Most vaccines are kept at 2°C to 8°C during storage and transport. This range protects vaccines from heat while preventing accidental freezing. Some vaccines tolerate freezing, but many are damaged by it. Cold chain failure can reduce vaccine potency without visible change.

Immunization & EPI.question: 33) Vaccine vial monitor is mainly used to detect:
Immunization & EPI.option4: Exposure of vaccine to cumulative heat
Immunization & EPI.exp: Vaccine vial monitor changes with cumulative heat exposure. It helps health workers decide whether a vaccine can still be used. It is especially useful during outreach sessions and transport. It does not primarily detect freezing damage.

Immunization & EPI.question: 34) Freeze-sensitive vaccines include:
Immunization & EPI.option1: DPT-containing vaccines and hepatitis B-containing vaccines
Immunization & EPI.exp: Many adsorbed vaccines are damaged by freezing. DPT-containing vaccines and hepatitis B-containing vaccines are freeze-sensitive. Freezing can cause loss of potency and increased local reaction. Shake test may be used when freezing damage is suspected.

Immunization & EPI.question: 35) Herd immunity means protection of susceptible persons because:
Immunization & EPI.exp: Herd immunity reduces transmission when a large proportion of the community is immune. This indirectly protects susceptible individuals. It is important for diseases transmitted from person to person. High vaccination coverage is needed to maintain herd effect.

Immunization & EPI.question: 36) Active immunity after vaccination is produced by:
Immunization & EPI.exp: Vaccination stimulates the host’s own immune system. This produces active immunity with memory response. Protection may take time to develop. It differs from passive immunity, where ready-made antibody is given.

Immunization & EPI.question: 37) Passive immunity is produced by:
Immunization & EPI.exp: Passive immunity occurs when ready-made antibodies are given or transferred. It gives rapid but temporary protection. Examples include immunoglobulin administration and maternal antibody transfer. It does not usually produce long-term immune memory.

Immunization & EPI.question: 38) BCG is usually given by which route?
Immunization & EPI.exp: BCG is given intradermally. It is commonly administered over the upper arm. Correct technique is important to produce proper local reaction. Wrong route may increase complications or reduce effectiveness.

Immunization & EPI.question: 39) OPV is given by:
Immunization & EPI.exp: OPV means oral polio vaccine. It is a live attenuated vaccine. It is given by mouth and can induce intestinal immunity.

Immunization & EPI.question: 40) IPV is usually given by:
Immunization & EPI.exp: IPV is inactivated polio vaccine. Unlike OPV, it is not given orally. It is administered by injection.

Immunization & EPI.question: 41) Penta vaccine protects against diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, hepatitis B and:
Immunization & EPI.exp: Pentavalent vaccine contains five antigens. It protects against diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, hepatitis B and Hib. This reduces multiple injections into one combined vaccine. It is part of the infant EPI schedule.

Immunization & EPI.question: 42) MR vaccine protects against:
Immunization & EPI.exp: MR means measles-rubella vaccine. It is a combined vaccine. In the file, MR-1 is at 9 months and MR-2 is at 15 months.

Immunization & EPI.question: 43) The first three primary infant EPI visits after birth occur at:
Immunization & EPI.exp: After birth dose, infant EPI visits occur at 6, 10 and 14 weeks. These visits include Penta, OPV and PCV doses. IPV is included at 6 and 14 weeks

Immunization & EPI.question: 44) Which vaccine is given both at 6 weeks and 14 weeks but not at 10 weeks in the schedule?
Immunization & EPI.exp: IPV-1 is given at 6 weeks. IPV-2 is given at 14 weeks. No IPV dose is listed at 10 weeks .

Immunization & EPI.question: 45) Which vaccine is listed at all three visits: 6, 10 and 14 weeks?
Immunization & EPI.exp: Penta-1, Penta-2 and Penta-3 are given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks. OPV and PCV are also given at these three visits. MR is given later at 9 and 15 months.

Immunization & EPI.question: 46) OPV doses are listed at:
Immunization & EPI.exp: OPV-1, OPV-2 and OPV-3 are listed at 6, 10 and 14 weeks. The file does not list OPV at 9 months. MR is given at 9 months.

Immunization & EPI.question: 47) PCV doses are given at:
Immunization & EPI.exp: PCV-1, PCV-2 and PCV-3 are given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks. PCV is classified as extracted cellular fraction vaccine. It is part of infant EPI schedule.

Immunization & EPI.question: 48) Which pair is correctly matched?
Immunization & EPI.exp: MR-2 is given at 15 months. MR-1 is given at 9 months. BCG is given at birth and IPV-2 at 14 weeks.

Immunization & EPI.question: 49) Which visit contains four vaccines ?
Immunization & EPI.exp: At 6 weeks, Penta-1, OPV-1, PCV-1 and IPV-1 are given. At 10 weeks, three vaccines are listed. At birth and 15 months, one vaccine is listed.

Immunization & EPI.question: 50) Which visit contains only BCG in the schedule?
Immunization & EPI.exp: At birth, BCG is listed in the EPI schedule. The 6-week visit includes multiple vaccines. MR vaccines are given later.

Immunization & EPI.question: 51) Which of the following is not a routine vaccine but is included under EPI Plus child service?
Immunization & EPI.exp: Vitamin A capsule is included under EPI Plus for under-5 children. It is not a vaccine. It is provided using the EPI platform for child health benefit.

Immunization & EPI.question: 52) Sex education under EPI Plus is grouped under:
Immunization & EPI.exp: Sex education is listed under couple/mother services. The same group includes breastfeeding advice and family planning advice. These services use EPI contact opportunities.

Immunization & EPI.question: 53) The main purpose of cold chain is to maintain:
Immunization & EPI.exp: Cold chain maintains vaccine potency from manufacturer to recipient. Vaccines are biological products and can be damaged by heat or freezing. A vaccine may look normal even after potency loss. So correct storage and transport temperature is essential.

Immunization & EPI.question: 54) A child receiving Penta-2, OPV-2 and PCV-2 is most likely attending which EPI visit?
Immunization & EPI.exp: Penta-2, OPV-2 and PCV-2 are given at 10 weeks. At 6 weeks, first doses are given with IPV-1. At 14 weeks, third doses are given with IPV-2.

Immunization & EPI.question: 55) A child receiving MR-1 is most likely aged:
Immunization & EPI.exp: MR-1 is given at 9 months. MR-2 is given at 15 months. This distinction is important in routine immunization recall.
